title: The marginal value of the next dollar

questions.heading: The Next $1k Is Worth Nothing at Most Budgets, and a Jump at a Few
questions.stem: Every project in a portfolio costs a whole multiple of $25k, and the current budget, $4,500k, is one too. What is the next $10k worth to the MILP?

options.text: Nothing, since no plan can cost strictly between two multiples of $25k
options.says: Right: every plan's cost is a multiple of $25k, so V cannot step before $4,525k.

options.text: The relaxation's price times 10, since a small change follows the price
options.says: The relaxation's price predicted $0.30k to $0.72k for the next $1k; the MILP gained 0 at all six budgets.

options.text: A full step, since every $10k crosses at least one plan's cost
options.says: With costs in $25k units, a $10k change crosses no plan's cost from here.

options.text: The fixed-integer price times 10, since the plan stays as it is
options.says: With no continuous variable to buy, a fixed plan has no use for money at all.

questions.heading: Over $1,000k the LP Price Is About Right; Over $100k It Is Not
questions.stem: At a budget of $52,000k the LP relaxation's budget price is 0.41. Finance wants two figures: the worth of +$80k and the worth of +$2,000k. How should you use the price?

options.text: For both: a price times the change is right for any change
options.says: Over $100k the MILP's gain was up to three times the price's forecast.

options.text: For neither: an LP price says nothing about a MILP's value
options.says: Over $1,000k the price came within 12% of the MILP's gain at six budgets.

options.text: For +$2,000k as a rough figure; re-solve for +$80k
options.says: Right: a large change crosses many steps and averages out; a small one does not.

options.text: For +$80k as a rough figure; re-solve for +$2,000k
options.says: It is the small change the price gets wrong, not the large one.

questions.heading: Tell Finance the Steps, Not a Rate
questions.stem: From $30,000k the step points are (30,000, 18,240), (30,060, 18,262) and (30,410, 18,301). Finance asks, in one sentence, what +$400k buys.

options.text: +$400k buys $61k, the rise to the last step listed
options.says: The last step is at $30,410k, past $30,400k, so it is not bought.
Right: V(30,400) is 18,262, one step above 18,240.
The step at $30,060k lies inside the $400k and is bought.
The gain is $22k in all, from one step, not a rate per $100k.
